Issued at 1255 AM CDT Thu Aug 13 2026

Current Overnight - Today:

During the current overnight hours through this morning, remnant 
convective activity over the eastern Dakotas and west-central and 
southern Minnesota will slide east through central/southern 
Minnesota into Wisconsin. This will bring some chances for isolated 
to scattered showers and perhaps an embedded thunderstorm or two to 
primarily southern portions of the Northland, particularly the 
Brainerd Lakes into northwest Wisconsin and areas south. With 
limited instability and the main forcing with a passing weak 
shortwave remaining to our south, no severe weather is expected.
Most areas will not see measurable rain, and those that do 
should only see a few hundredths to a tenth of an inch or two at
best. Patchy fog is also possible early this morning, mainly in
northeast Minnesota. Widespread dense fog is not expected.

As the shortwave to our south pushes east throughout the day today, 
areas of clouds should persist, especially in the southern half of 
the Northland. Can't rule out a few sprinkles or stray showers in 
inland northwest Wisconsin into the afternoon, but chances are low 
(around 20% or less). Otherwise, expect a seasonal day today with 
high temperatures in the mid-70s to low-80s for most locations along 
with fairly light northeast winds. The funneling of these winds into 
the head of Lake Superior may lead to a moderate risk for rip 
currents at Minnesota and Wisconsin Point beaches late this 
afternoon and evening. Smoke aloft will also keep skies hazy where 
clouds clear.

Friday - Saturday:

Most of Friday is forecast to remain dry as a shortwave ridge and 
surface high pressure influence the region. The surface pressure 
gradient will be on the increase throughout Friday as weakly forced 
shortwave energy on the western side of the shortwave ridge and
an associated surface low pressure system will be moving into 
the Dakotas. This will drive increasing northeast winds off of 
Lake Superior, leading to a likely risk of rip currents at 
Minnesota and Wisconsin Point beaches Friday through Friday 
evening. High temperatures will be similar to Thursday in the 
mid-70s to mid-80s, though slightly cooler near Lake Superior.

Starting as early as Friday night and continuing into Saturday 
morning, isentropic upglide/warm-air advection ahead of the 
approaching low pressure system will bring areas of scattered 
showers and embedded thunderstorms into the Northland. Additional 
isolated to scattered showers and embedded thunderstorm activity 
continues through much of Saturday on a scattered basis along and 
ahead of the cold front that will be moving west to east across the 
area. Medium-range ensembles vary on the exact timing of this 
system, some bringing precipitation in as early as Friday night and 
some bringing it in later towards Saturday morning or afternoon. 
Given the fairly weak forcing associated with the shortwave trough 
and marginal instability into the Northland with this system, severe 
weather is not expected at this time. Global ensembles as a whole 
are tame regarding precipitation amounts with this system, with most 
only up to one quarter of an inch or less. In fact, NBM 
probabilities for 0.25" or greater are only above 50% (i.e. 50-70%) 
in portions of Itasca, far northern St. Louis, and Koochiching 
counties in north-central Minnesota with lower chances elsewhere. 
These same locations have a 30-40% probability for greater than 0.5" 
and a less than 20% chance for greater than 1". The higher 
accumulations would only be attainable for areas that see several 
thunderstorms move overhead.

Saturday will be a couple degrees cooler than Friday, with high 
temperatures forecast in the low-70s to low-80s, though slightly 
cooler near Lake Superior.

Early to Mid-Next Week:

Most of the first half of next week will see a broader zonal to 
slightly northwest flow pattern aloft, with periodic embedded 
shortwave trough energy at times that could bring additional shower 
and thunderstorm chances (30-60%) in the late Monday through mid-
week timeframe. However, confidence in exact timing, locations, and 
amounts is lower at this time range. Temperatures for the first half 
of next week are forecast to remain around normal with highs in the 
70s to low-80s and overnight lows in the 50s to low-60s.
